title: Tokenisation of Financial Markets
summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess tokenised securities, funds and collateral, DLT market infrastructure, settlement finality, custody and smart contract risk.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to oversee the tokenisation of securities, funds and collateral: assessing legal certainty, DLT market infrastructure, settlement finality, custody and smart contract risk, and applying familiar regulatory principles to new market structures.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a practical, technology-neutral understanding of how traditional financial assets are tokenised, issued, traded, settled and held on distributed ledgers, and where the risks lie. Participants leave able to assess tokenisation initiatives and DLT infrastructures against established principles, identify red flags and shape the authority's approach to pilots and wider adoption.
sections.What It Covers: Tokenisation and DLT foundations, the legal basis of tokenised assets, tokenised securities, tokenised funds, tokenised collateral, DLT market infrastructure, settlement finality and the PFMI, custody and segregation, interoperability and smart contract risk, and pilot regimes and supervisory strategy.
Intended Audience: Supervisors of investment firms, trading venues, fund managers, custodians and market infrastructures
Central bank and market infrastructure oversight staff dealing with DLT-based settlement
Policy, legal and innovation teams assessing tokenisation proposals, sandboxes and pilot regimes
Learning Objectives: Explain how tokenisation works and how DLT-based markets differ from traditional infrastructure
Assess the legal certainty of tokenised assets, including ownership, transfer and finality
Evaluate tokenised securities, funds and collateral arrangements against existing regulatory requirements
Apply the PFMI and custody principles to DLT-based trading, settlement and safekeeping
Identify interoperability, smart contract and operational risks and the evidence to request from firms
Design a supervisory approach to tokenisation pilots, sandboxes and wider market adoption
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies, red flags and supervisory question exercises, closing with a review of a tokenisation proposal, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: A basic understanding of crypto-assets and blockchain is helpful, for example from a fundamentals course, together with some experience of securities, funds or market infrastructure supervision. No technical background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Tokenisation (2024)
CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
BIS, Annual Economic Report 2023, Chapter III: Blueprint for the Future Monetary System

modules.title: Foundations of Tokenisation and Distributed Ledgers
modules.summary: What tokenisation means in practice, the distributed ledger designs that support it, and the efficiency, transparency and programmability claims that drive market interest.
objectives: Explain the process of tokenising a traditional financial asset
Distinguish permissioned and permissionless ledgers and their governance
Assess claimed benefits of tokenisation against current market practice
syllabus: Tokens, ledgers, nodes and consensus in plain language
Permissioned and permissionless networks: governance and access
Asset classes being tokenised: bonds, funds, equities and real assets
Claimed benefits: atomic settlement, fractionalisation and programmability

modules.title: The Legal Basis of Tokenised Assets
modules.summary: How the law recognises ownership and transfer of tokenised assets, the difference between digitally native and digital twin structures, and why legal certainty is the first supervisory question.
objectives: Explain how tokenised assets are characterised under securities and property law
Distinguish digitally native issuance from tokenised representations of existing assets
Assess the legal risks arising from mismatches between the ledger and the legal record
syllabus: Native tokens, digital twins and depositary receipt structures
Classification: when is a token a financial instrument
Ledger records, registers of ownership and conflict of laws
Insolvency, enforceability and investor rights

modules.title: Tokenised Securities and Primary Markets
modules.summary: How tokenised bonds and equities are issued, disclosed and distributed, the roles of issuers, arrangers and platform operators, and the investor protection issues supervisors should test.
objectives: Explain the issuance process for tokenised bonds and equities
Assess disclosure, prospectus and distribution requirements for tokenised offerings
Evaluate investor protection risks from fractionalisation and retail access
syllabus: Tokenised bond issuance by sovereigns, supranationals and corporates
Roles of issuers, arrangers, registrars and token platforms
Disclosure of technology, legal and operational risks
Fractionalisation, retail distribution and suitability

modules.title: Tokenised Funds and Fund Distribution
modules.summary: How fund units, including money market fund shares, are being tokenised, the effect on transfer agency, valuation and distribution, and the supervisory questions for fund managers and depositaries.
objectives: Explain how tokenised fund units are issued, transferred and redeemed
Assess the implications for transfer agency, valuation and investor registers
Evaluate liquidity and conduct risks of tokenised money market fund shares
syllabus: Tokenised share classes and on-chain transfer agency
NAV calculation, dealing cycles and redemption on a ledger
Tokenised money market fund shares as collateral and settlement assets
Responsibilities of managers, depositaries and distributors

modules.title: Tokenised Collateral and Repo
modules.summary: How tokenisation is being used to mobilise collateral, support intraday repo and margining, and the legal, operational and liquidity risks that faster collateral movements create.
objectives: Explain the use of tokenised assets in collateral management and repo
Assess legal enforceability of collateral arrangements on a ledger
Evaluate liquidity and procyclicality risks of faster collateral mobility
syllabus: Collateral mobility, intraday repo and margin calls
Collateral eligibility, haircuts and valuation of tokenised assets
Enforceability, close-out netting and default management
Interaction with central counterparties and margin frameworks

modules.title: DLT Market Infrastructure: Trading, Clearing and Settlement
modules.summary: How DLT-based trading venues and settlement systems are structured, how the cash leg is settled, and how supervisors assess combined trading and settlement models.
objectives: Explain DLT-based trading, clearing and settlement models
Assess cash leg options, from tokenised deposits to wholesale central bank money
Evaluate conflicts and risks in combined trading and settlement functions
syllabus: DLT trading venues and multilateral settlement systems
Delivery versus payment and atomic settlement
Cash leg options: central bank money, tokenised deposits and stablecoins
Disintermediation, vertical integration and conflicts of interest

modules.title: Settlement Finality and the PFMI
modules.summary: Why settlement finality is fundamental to market stability, how it is achieved on distributed ledgers with different consensus models, and how the PFMI apply to DLT-based infrastructure.
objectives: Explain legal and operational settlement finality
Assess probabilistic finality and rollback risk in different ledger designs
Apply the PFMI to DLT-based payment, settlement and securities systems
syllabus: Legal finality, operational finality and the irrevocability of transfers
Consensus mechanisms, forks and probabilistic finality
PFMI principles on governance, settlement, operational and liquidity risk
CPMI and IOSCO guidance on stablecoin and DLT arrangements

modules.title: Custody, Safekeeping and Asset Segregation
modules.summary: How custody changes when assets are held as tokens, from private key management and wallet architecture to segregation, reconciliation and the protection of client assets on insolvency.
objectives: Explain custody models for tokenised assets and the role of private keys
Assess segregation, reconciliation and client asset protection on a ledger
Evaluate key management controls and the risk of loss or theft
syllabus: Custody models: direct holding, omnibus and third-party custodians
Private key management, multi-signature and threshold signatures
Reconciliation between on-chain records and books and records
Insolvency protection and return of client assets

modules.title: Interoperability, Smart Contracts and Technology Risk
modules.summary: The technology risks specific to tokenised markets, including fragmented ledgers, cross-chain bridges, oracles and smart contract vulnerabilities, and the evidence supervisors should request from firms.
objectives: Assess interoperability between ledgers and with traditional infrastructure
Evaluate smart contract risk, code audits and upgrade governance
Identify operational, cyber and third-party risks in DLT arrangements
syllabus: Fragmentation, cross-chain bridges and messaging standards
Smart contract vulnerabilities, audits and emergency controls
Oracles, data feeds and node operator dependencies
Red flags and supervisory questions on DLT technology risk

modules.title: Pilot Regimes, Sandboxes and Supervisory Strategy
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a strategic view of how authorities enable and oversee tokenisation, from sandboxes and pilot regimes to permanent frameworks and international coordination.
objectives: Compare sandbox, pilot regime and permanent framework approaches to tokenisation
Evaluate a tokenisation initiative against supervisory and financial stability criteria
Design the authority's approach to tokenised markets
syllabus: Pilot regimes and sandboxes: exemptions, limits and exit routes
Lessons from tokenisation pilots and central bank experiments
International work: FSB, IOSCO, CPMI and BIS on tokenisation
Workshop: supervisory review of a tokenised bond and settlement proposal

related.title: Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals
related.summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving supervisors a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks they must supervise.

related.title: Crypto-Asset Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An advanced twelve-module programme equipping supervisors to authorise, supervise and take action against crypto-asset firms under comprehensive regimes and international standards.

related.title: Digital Money: Stablecoins, Tokenised Deposits and CBDCs
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and central bankers to assess stablecoins, tokenised deposits and CBDCs, and their risks to payments and financial stability.

related.title: MiCA Essentials for Supervisors (EU Edition)
related.summary: A six-module essentials programme giving EU national competent authority staff a practical command of MiCA, from token regimes and CASP authorisation to supervision and enforcement.

related.title: Supervising Crypto-Asset Service Providers under MiCA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An advanced fifteen-module programme equipping EU national competent authorities to authorise and supervise crypto-asset service providers and token issuers under MiCA.

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.
